checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the primary subject (hockey puck) is completely absent from the image. Consequently, marking all specific geometric and functional checkpoints for the puck as 'is_testable: false' is logically sound because there is no object to test. The only testable checkpoint ('Ice hockey game equipment') was correctly marked as present due to the player and stick. The Router was not lenient; it accurately reflected the total failure of the generation to include the target class.
artifact_review: The Router's identification of 'missing_parts' with severity 5 is accurate and critical. The absence of the class-defining object is a catastrophic alignment failure. The Router also noted structural issues with the stick (severity 3) and texture anomalies on the player (severity 2). The experts support this: the open_vocabulary_detector found zero pucks, confirming the missing part. The topology auditor confirmed the stick is a single entity but didn't rule out the boundary melting noted by the Router. The perceptual auditor noted slight blur. The severity of the missing puck outweighs all other artifacts.
alignment_reasoning: The image fails to contain the target class object ('puck'). While the fine_grained_classifier predicted 'puck' with high confidence (likely due to the context of the hockey player and stick), the open_vocabulary_detector definitively confirmed the absence of any bounding box for a puck. An image labeled 'puck' that contains no puck is a fundamental alignment failure. The score is near zero because the primary subject is missing.
artifact_reasoning: The primary artifact is the complete omission of the target object (Severity 5). Secondary artifacts include slight structural ambiguity in the hockey stick blade (Severity 3) and minor textural blurring on the player (Severity 2). The mask provided by the topology auditor shows a clean segmentation of the player/stick, but this does not compensate for the missing puck. The artifact score is low (good) relative to the visual quality of the *present* elements, but the missing object is a structural defect.
